children: Gold futures have fallen for four straight sessions, and Forex.com analyst Fawad Razaqzada sees room for further declines, saying precious metals could continue to struggle as elevated oil prices drive inflation pressures higher.

"One of the main reasons why gold and other low- and zero-yielding assets have come under pressure is due to the fact bond markets are slumping," Razaqzada said in his latest precious metals note, as 10-year Treasury yields have pushed above 5% and 30-year yields are testing levels last reached in 2007.

"Gold typically goes up when yields go down, as the opportunity cost of holding the zero-yielding asset decreases. And when yields rise, gold typically heads lower for the same reason," the analyst said.
Adding to the bearish fundamental outlook, Razaqzada said gold also faces growing technical headwinds as traders who went long during the August rally are now trapped.

But market sentiment is fluid and can quickly change, Razaqzada said, and "if investors lose faith in the Fed and its ability to control inflation or yields, then the dollar debasement trade could resurface, [which] could be positive for gold, silver, and bitcoin, as well as currencies of countries with better fiscal discipline."

Gold futures extended losses on Thursday as the market remains pressured by strong gains in the dollar and U.S. yields, with a high probability of an October Federal Reserve rate hike; traders are now pricing a 69% chance of a rate hike in October, according to CME's FedWatch ​Tool.
